root_cause.parser_behaviour: Splits <geoReference> on spaces, recognises ONLY +lat_0 and +lon_0, and if either is NaN logs a warning then substitutes latitude=42.0 longitude=2.0.
root_cause.evidence_of_selective_defect: 44 .xodr files carry a geoReference; 42 contain BOTH +lat_0 and +lon_0. The only 2 that do not are the two Ingolstadt maps. Every stock CARLA town map is complete.
root_cause.measured_impact: Fallback places the map at lat 42.0 lon 2.0; Ingolstadt is lat ~48.766 lon ~11.425. ~6.77 deg latitude, ~9.43 deg longitude, roughly 752 km. Every runtime get_location()/GNSS/perception geolocation would be silently wrong.

DECISIVE_OBSERVATION_two_pass_rebuild.finding: The import ran the governed tile sequence TWICE inside the truncated run.
DECISIVE_OBSERVATION_two_pass_rebuild.deduplicated_total: 7.42 h across 21 distinct meshes (vs 8.77 h logged)
why_this_matters: The same governed tiles are imported more than once per run, so distance fields are rebuilt for the same assets.
The second build of each mesh is only ~10% cheaper. A pure DDC miss would make the second pass near-zero, so cache warmth does NOT explain the cost.
This is direct evidence for the log's own hint that the mesh is rebuilt excessively.
